title: World Athletics Road Running Championships Copenhagen 26: summary of six individual-event reports (mile, 5km, half marathon)
weather: Half marathon report (men): a bright morning. Women's 5km report: a cool afternoon, with the winner noting some wind but manageable conditions. Mile report (men): the winner sheltered from the wind.

story.W: Mile: Agathe Guillemot waited in a big lead group, moved to the front with about 20 seconds left and won in a European record 4:22.74. 5km: Likina Amebaw took control early, made her decisive move at 4 km away from Caroline Gitonga and won by seven seconds in 14:41. Half marathon: Agnes Ngetich led from the start, was 51 seconds clear at 20 km and won alone by 50 seconds in a women-only world record of 1:05:15 (subject to ratification).
story.M: Mile: Yared Nuguse led from the start aiming at the world record, but Robert Farken stayed close, closed from about 600 m out, passed him and won in 3:51.80. 5km: Dawit Seare and Jakob Ingebrigtsen broke clear; Ingebrigtsen went ahead with about 30 seconds left but Seare answered and won by 3 seconds in 12:56. Half marathon: Kenyans controlled the middle of the race, then Andreas Almgren, Nicholas Kipkorir and Joshua Cheptegei went clear; Almgren pulled away in the last stretch to win by 5 seconds in a European record 58:06.

performances.name: Agathe GUILLEMOT
performances.note: Mile champion in 4:22.74, a European record and fourth on the all-time list; her first individual global title after a demanding season.

performances.name: Freweyni HAILU
performances.note: Mile silver in 4:24.35, second again three years after her silver in Riga.

performances.name: Annemarie NISSEN
performances.note: Fourth in the mile with a personal best of 4:26.78, cheered by the home crowd.

performances.name: Likina AMEBAW
performances.note: Won the 5km in 14:41, six days after winning the Ultimate 5000m title.

performances.name: Caroline Makandi GITONGA
performances.note: Second in the 5km in 14:48; led for a spell and was dropped by Amebaw at 4 km. Report calls her Caroline Gitonga.

performances.name: Rose DAVIES
performances.note: Third in the 5km in 14:50, an Oceanian record.

performances.name: Agnes Jebet NGETICH
performances.note: Won the half marathon in 1:05:15, a women-only world record by one second, her second world title of 2026 after cross-country. Report calls her Agnes Ngetich.

performances.name: Veronica LOLEO
performances.note: Second in the half marathon in 1:06:05, 50 seconds behind her Kenyan teammate.

performances.name: Florence NIYONKURU
performances.note: Third in the half marathon in a Rwandan record 1:06:08.

performances.name: Tsigie GEBRESELAMA
performances.note: Dropped from the chase group around 15 km in the half marathon and did not reach the top ten.

performances.name: Jessica MCCLAIN
performances.note: Dropped from the chase group at 15 km in the half marathon but recovered to finish seventh.

performances.name: Robert FARKEN
performances.note: Mile champion in a world-leading German record 3:51.80, second on the all-time road mile list; his final race of the season.

performances.name: Yared NUGUSE
performances.note: Led the mile from the start chasing the world record; second in 3:52.33.

performances.name: Ruben QUERINJEAN
performances.note: Mile bronze in a Luxembourg record 3:52.77, the country's first men's global senior medal since 1952.

performances.name: Dawit SEARE
performances.note: Won the 5km in a national record 12:56 by outkicking Ingebrigtsen; fourth in Riga three years earlier.

performances.name: Jakob INGEBRIGTSEN
performances.note: Second in the 5km in a Norwegian record 12:59 on his 26th birthday; briefly took the lead with about 30 seconds left.

performances.name: Jimmy GRESSIER
performances.note: European record holder at 12:51 earlier in the year; led early in the 5km but was not in the top ten (report gives no explanation).

performances.name: Andreas ALMGREN
performances.note: Won the half marathon in a European record 58:06, 35 seconds faster than his own mark; first global gold, ninth on the all-time list.

performances.name: Nicholas KIPKORIR
performances.note: Second in the half marathon in 58:11 after leading much of the race; surged ahead briefly in the last 600 m.

performances.name: Joshua CHEPTEGEI
performances.note: Third in the half marathon in a personal best 58:26, his first road medal; fell off the front pair near Trianglen and said he had a treated foot problem.

performances.name: Tadese WORKU
performances.note: Fourth in the half marathon in a personal best 58:35; dropped before 20 km.

performances.name: Daniel Simiu EBENYO
performances.note: Silver medallist in Riga, ran in the Kenyan group at the front early and finished ninth. Report calls him Daniel Ebenyo.
